subject.title: fix(slack): add default 30s timeout to read and write WebClients

question: Should every Slack mutating API call fail after 30 seconds even when OpenClaw cannot determine whether Slack committed the operation?
rationale: The correct write policy balances process availability against duplicate or falsely failed delivery, and neither the dependency nor current OpenClaw behavior defines that product tradeoff.

options.title: Scope to reads first
options.body: Apply the shared 30-second timeout to lookup and read clients, leaving generic writes unchanged until write-specific delivery semantics are designed.

options.title: Accept bounded writes
options.body: Approve the 30-second write deadline explicitly and require delayed-response proof plus documented ambiguous-delivery behavior before merge.

options.title: Split mutating operations
options.body: Apply deadlines only to idempotent writes and add idempotency or reconciliation for message creation before bounding chat.postMessage.

recommendation.title: Scope to reads first
recommendation.body: Apply the shared 30-second timeout to lookup and read clients, leaving generic writes unchanged until write-specific delivery semantics are designed.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work introduced the exact read/write resolver boundary now being changed.
